summary: Allowed Herman Gluck, a deputy collector of internal revenue at New York whose service ended March 1, 1907, to be reinstated even though his year of eligibility had expired.
Let George Terwilliger return to the Government Printing Office regardless of how long he had been out of the service.
Permitted William E. Shields to be reinstated in the Government Printing Office no matter how long he had been away.
Amended Executive Order 503, which authorized extra pay for messmen in the Marine Corps.
Withdrew additional tracts inside the Gila National Forest, just north of Fort Bayard, for military use to protect the fort's water supply, while keeping the land part of the national forest.
Set apart a tract of public land at Tanana, next to the Fort Gibbon military reservation, as a military reservation for the Army Signal Corps.
Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission until March 2, 1909, to finish its work.

Changed the rules for hiring unskilled laborers in federal offices outside Washington, D.C., so the Civil Service Commission could keep eligible registers in force longer than one year when the service required it.
Carried out a land swap with Porto Rico: unneeded parts of an 80-acre naval tract on the Caguas road in San Juan went to the island government, which in turn ceded three tracts to the United States.

Created the Key West Reservation, setting aside the keys and islands of the Florida Keys west of Key West as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, without disturbing existing life-saving and naval reservations there.

Established the Klamath Lake Reservation, reserving the islands of Lower Klamath Lake and nearby marsh lands unfit for farming as a breeding ground for native birds, and banned killing birds or taking their eggs and nests.
Designated Assistant Attorney General George W. Woodruff to act as Secretary of the Interior when the Secretary is absent.
Gave per diem employees and day laborers across the federal service the first Monday in September, Labor Day, off as a full holiday.
Put a commercial agreement with the Netherlands into effect, cutting U.S. duties on Dutch brandies and other distilled spirits to the reduced reciprocity rate.
Extended the military reservations on Batan Island and Cacraray Island in the Philippines to take in the submerged lands, reefs and rocks out to 1,000 yards beyond low water.
Amended the Canal Zone Penal Code so grand larceny carries up to ten years in the penitentiary.
Created the Lake Malheur Reservation, protecting the shorelines, islands and connecting waters of Lakes Malheur and Harney as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Authorized an advance of funds to Capt. Albert Mertz to move Lighthouse Establishment vessels to the Pacific coast.
Opened unallotted Rosebud Indian Reservation lands south of the Big White River to homestead settlement on March 1, 1909, setting out rules for registration and the drawing.
Allowed Harry H. Weddle of California to be appointed inspector in charge at San Diego in the Immigration Service without a civil-service examination.
Established the Chase Lake Reservation, reserving public lands within Chase Lake's meander lines as a breeding ground for native birds, where taking birds, eggs or nests is prohibited.
Exempted civilian professors, instructors and teachers at the Military Academy at West Point and the Naval Academy at Annapolis from civil-service examination.
Reserved additional South Dakota lands within the Belle Fourche Irrigation Project for agricultural experiments.
Allowed Frank Dingman, C. W. G. Brett, Raymond Bartlett and Charles F. Young to be hired for tabulating statistics in the Bureau of the Census without civil-service rules.
Reserved a parcel of land in California for lighthouse purposes.

Created an Interdepartmental Statistical Committee, with a member from each executive department and the Interstate Commerce Commission, to make government statistics uniform and cut duplicate work. Lawrence O. Murray was named chairman.
Set aside the Tumacacori Mission ruins, a Spanish mission in Santa Cruz County, and the ten acres beneath them as the Tumacacori National Monument.
Allowed Drs. Hopkins and Cunningham to be appointed, without civil-service rules, as physicians teaching microscopic work on tropical diseases at Ancon Hospital on the Isthmus of Panama.
Created the Pine Island Reservation, protecting Bird Island, Middle Island and another small islet near the north end of Pine Island Sound as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Permitted Albert W. Pontius of Minnesota to be appointed a class-three clerk in the Department of State without examination.
Allowed customs officer Charles H. Cameron to transfer to Chinese inspector in the Immigration Service without examination.
Reserved a small island in Palma Sola Bay as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, prohibiting the taking of birds, eggs or nests except under Agriculture Department rules.
Created the Matlacha Pass Reservation, setting aside four small islands in Matlacha Pass as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Let George Shaffer, Olof Ekedahl and Willoughby Culbertson stay on clerical duties in the Isthmian Canal Service without civil-service examination.
Reserved a 0.71-acre tract at Circle for an Army Signal Corps wireless telegraph station serving Alaska's telegraph lines.
Allowed Melvin W. Sheppard to be appointed a night inspector in the customs service at the port of Philadelphia without meeting civil-service rules.
Exempted one inspecting engineer and the inspectors in the Isthmian Canal Commission's purchasing department from civil-service examination.
Brought eight people employed jointly by the Isthmian Canal Commission and the Panama Railroad Company into the Commission's classified force when the two offices' work was separated.
Broadened the civil-service retransfer rule so employees who had served continuously in the judicial as well as executive service could return to a former position.
Allowed employees hired outside the civil-service rules before a February 12, 1908, Attorney General opinion to be classified with Civil Service Commission approval, with limits on their transfer.
Allowed Captain William Norman to be appointed assistant inspector of hulls in the Steamboat-Inspection Service at New Orleans without examination.
Permitted John A. Flickinger, three times certified from the watchman register, to be appointed a watchman in the classified service.
Added a rule letting the Civil Service Commission approve demoting classified employees to unskilled laborer and transferring laborers between offices outside Washington, D.C.
Exempted civilian instructors in the Revenue-Cutter Service from civil-service examination.
Gave the labor board in Washington, D.C., authority to approve demotions to unskilled laborer and, in urgent cases, temporary laborer appointments longer than thirty days.
Allowed Frederick Koch to be appointed disciplinarian at the Carlisle Indian School after a noncompetitive examination.
Let Conrad Henzman, a retired first sergeant with thirty years in the Army, be appointed messenger at military headquarters in New York City without examination.
Created the Island Bay Reservation, setting aside unsurveyed mangrove and other islands in a Florida township as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Permitted Mary A. Eldridge to be reinstated as a clerk in the office of the Auditor for the War Department, based on her earlier Patent Office service.
Reserved the northern part of Montague Point on Montague Island, where U.S. cables land, for the Army Signal Corps' military telegraph lines in Alaska.
Created the Loch-Katrine Reservation, setting aside a reservoir site in Wyoming's Oregon Basin, plus a 50-foot strip around it, as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Reserved land at Makanalua on the island of Molokai for lighthouse purposes.
Allowed Charles W. Edwards, an unclassified laborer in the office of the Register of the Treasury, to be made a classified laborer in the Treasury Department.
Set apart Thursday, November 26, 1908, as a national day of thanksgiving.
Redrew the boundaries of Parcel B of the Malate Barracks military reservation in Manila.
Reserved certain lands at Susitna and Tyonic for educational purposes.
Set new procedures for defendants appealing Canal Zone District Court judgments, including notice deadlines and bond limits, and repealed certain sections of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Narrowed the Isthmian Canal Commission's civil-service exception so employees classified in 1904 into competitive positions are not covered by it on transfer.
Allowed Hilworth T. B. Jones to be appointed a translator at $1,400 a year in the Office of Naval Intelligence without civil-service rules.

Assigned the Marine Corps its duties: garrisoning navy yards and naval stations, defending overseas naval bases, garrisoning the Isthmian Canal Zone, and furnishing expeditionary forces abroad in peacetime.
Withdrew two more tracts within the Gila National Forest for military use to protect Fort Bayard's water supply, keeping both reservations in force together.
Let three laborers hired at San Francisco after the 1906 earthquake and fire stay on with regular status, and allowed the Civil Service Commission to retain others hired the same way.
Allowed George F. Cooke to be reinstated to a post-office clerkship paying up to $1,000, regardless of the reinstatement time limit.
Excused Civil War veterans and members of the Women's Relief Corps and Sons of Veterans in federal service from duty on November 25, 1908, for the unveiling of the Philip Henry Sheridan statue.
Abolished the Dardanelle land district in Arkansas and folded it into the Little Rock land district.
Returned a tract set aside for the Chehalis Indians to the public domain and directed that it be allotted to Ada McKay, a Skokomish Indian.
Created the Ocala National Forest from partly timbered public lands in Florida, reserving them from settlement for the use and benefit of the people.
Established the Dakota National Forest on partly timbered public lands in North Dakota, reserving them from settlement and entry.
Cut the number of General Land Office special agents exempted from examination, who investigate fraudulent land entries, from five to three.
Barred most federal employees who are notaries public from charging fees for notarial acts done for government business or during office hours, on pain of dismissal.
Reserved land on Round Top (Ualakaa) and other Oahu sites, with rights-of-way, for observation stations tied to the island's defensive works.
Set apart a tract on the north side of the Gulkana River, near the Gulkana Telegraph Station, for the Army Signal Corps' military telegraph lines.
Revised the peacetime limits of punishment for Army enlisted men, capping confinement at hard labor for desertion at three years, with set conditions for modifying that limit.
Allowed Stephen C. Stuntz to be appointed soil bibliographer in the Agriculture Department's Bureau of Soils without civil-service rules.
Set apart the Choctawhatchee National Forest on partly timbered public lands in Florida.
Narrowed a civil-service exception covering star-route employees and post offices without city delivery to fourteen northern and northeastern states, excluding fourth-class postmasters.
Let the Post-Office Department fill newly classified fourth-class postmaster vacancies without examination until the Civil Service Commission could certify eligibles.
Opened civil-service examinations to deaf-mutes for any classified position the Civil Service Commission judged they could perform.
Enlarged the Camp Overton military reservation at Nonucan, near Iligan on Mindanao, to add land for a target range.
Rewrote the civil-service exception for the Army transport service, covering longshoremen, Philippine trade workers and most ship crews, and set conditions on later transfers or promotions.
Permitted Dell A. Baker to be appointed deputy collector in the office of the collector of customs at the port of New York.
Reserved for lighthouse purposes the U.S.-owned land on the island of Puukii at the entrance to Hana harbor, Maui.
Reserved a parcel at Lae o Kokole, in the Waimea district of Kauai, for lighthouse purposes, with a right-of-way to the government road.
Set aside land at McGregor's Point, in Maui's Lahaina district, for a lighthouse site and a keeper's dwelling site.
Reserved land at Kahala Point on Kauai for lighthouse purposes, along with a right-of-way to the Anahola wharf landing.
Reserved about 10 acres at Ka Lae, in the Kau district of the island of Hawaii, for lighthouse purposes.
Created the Wheeler National Monument to protect volcanic formations of unusual scientific interest within the Rio Grande and Cochetopa National Forests, making the monument the dominant reservation.
Abolished the Colby land district in Kansas and transferred its business to the Topeka land district.
Required Marine Corps officers to pass physical examinations and tests at least every two years, including a 90-mile, three-day riding test for field officers.
Allowed Georgia M. Sargent, widow of Commissioner-General of Immigration Frank P. Sargent, to be appointed to a classified position without examination.
Amended an earlier order so Wilhelm Lutz, assistant chief of police of Porto Rico, could be appointed to the U.S. Customs Service instead of the Immigration Bureau.
Allowed Walter R. Gallaher, an $1,800 clerk in the Isthmian service, to transfer to a classified clerical position in the United States.
Permitted Herman W. Kuchmeister, an assistant weigher in the Boston customs service, to be promoted to day inspector without further examination.
Allowed Clare Kiggins to be appointed to the departmental classified service after an appropriate noncompetitive examination.

Let civilians employed temporarily in Cuba under the provisional government or the Army of Cuban Pacification transfer into the U.S. classified service within a year, if they passed the entrance exam and met service conditions.
